en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who sent his falcon or his dog (to hunt), so it seized a prey, and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, whatever the falcon killed so do not eat from it except if you slaughter it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sends his falcon or dog to catch a prey which then catches a prey and eats thereof; if he can use the remaining for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, do not use for food what the falcon kills, unless you slaughter it properly.’”
